subject: Request: custom uptime & latency commitment for Pylon Systems
messages:
From: Aisha Lewis <aisha.lewis@pylon-systems.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@pylon-systems.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Uptime & latency commitments for enterprise plan - Pylon

Hi Diego,

Thanks for taking this — Pylon is finalizing procurement for our enterprise contract and they have one ask before signing: a committed uptime and token-latency target with financial credits for violations. High level:

- Target uptime: 99.995% (annual)
- Latency: 95th percentile token generation latency < 150ms for our production traffic (avg seq length ~ 512 tokens)
- Requesting service credits scaling up to 6 months of billings for repeated violations

I attached the proposed SLA they sent (pylon-proposed-sla.pdf). They say this commitment is a gating factor for their procurement sign-off next week.

Can Redwood provide an exception/authorized commitment for this account? If we need to pair this with Dedicated/reserved capacity or a Private deployment, please call that out — they want to understand operational constraints and runbook/monitoring requirements.

Copying our procurement contact (contracts@pylon-systems.com) and Michael Yuan (engineering lead).

Thanks,
Aisha Lewis
Director, Strategic Accounts
Pylon Systems

Forwarding Pylon's request — ETA: they need a decision within ~7 business days.

Quick notes from my side:
- They want 99.995% uptime and tight p95 latency. That latency target is aggressive for hosted multi-tenant without dedicated capacity.
- Likely options: Dedicated reserved pool + prioritized routing, or Private deployment. Both have cost/ops implications (billing, capacity commit, maintenance windows).
- Legal will need to sign off on the credit cap and the SOW. Finance will want a cap on exposure.

Questions for the group:
1) Product/Infra: feasibility & recommended configuration (Hosted exception vs Dedicated vs Private). Include estimated monthly cost uplift and whether we can meet p95 150ms for their token/seq profile.
2) Ops/Support: runbook/monitoring requirements and required SLIs/alerts.
3) Legal/Finance: acceptable credit cap (we should propose a maximum liability).

Attaching their proposed SLA for context.

Diego
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Uptime & latency commitments for enterprise plan - Pylon

Thanks for the ping, Diego — quick technical assessment from Product/Infra: 

Summary: P95 < 150ms at ~512 tokens with general-purpose hosted instances is unlikely without dedicated capacity and quantization/optimizations tailored to their workload. Meeting 99.995% annual uptime in the hosted environment would require a combination of: dedicated reserved pools, cross-region failover, and stricter maintenance window SLAs.

Recommended approach (feasible path):
- Offer Dedicated reserved capacity (per-customer GPU pool) with an SLA of 99.995% uptime subject to these constraints:
  - Customer must commit to a 12-month reserved capacity with a minimum monthly compute commit.
  - Scheduled maintenance windows limited to two per quarter, each no longer than 2 hours.
  - Dedicated pool is configured with autoscaling headroom and cross-AZ redundancy.
- For latency: we can meet p95 < 150ms for their traffic if we set:
  - Preferred model variants (quantized medium-latency kernels) and pinned model versions
  - Per-customer batching/queueing policy to prioritize production traffic

Operational requirements:
- Deliverable: availability runbook (draft attached) with escalation paths, monitoring dashboards, and SLO/SLA calculation methodology.
- SRE must own the 24x7 on-call rota for the dedicated pool; customer to have access to an uptime dashboard and token-level telemetry for the contract period.

Liability/credits: product suggests a cap of 3 months of recurring fees as an upper bound for financial exposure; anything above should be reviewed by Finance and Legal.

I've attached a first-pass runbook (availability-runbook-draft.md). If Legal/Finance are comfortable with the credit cap and the SOW is aligned, we can proceed with Laura/exec authorization.

- Hannah
Senior Product Manager, Availability
Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: availability-runbook-draft.md ---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Uptime & latency commitments for enterprise plan - Pylon

Approved in principle.

After reviewing Hannah's assessment and the runbook, I am comfortable granting a customer-specific uptime/latency commitment under the following conditions: 

- Delivery: Commitment limited to Dedicated reserved capacity with the configuration Hannah outlined (cross-AZ, autoscaling headroom).
- Maintenance: Scheduled maintenance limited to two 2-hour windows per quarter; unscheduled maintenance measured against agreed SLOs.
- Liability cap: Financial exposure capped at 3 months of recurring fees (per Product recommendation). Any request above that requires VP-level sign-off.
- SOW & Contract: Legal must include the runbook/monitoring links and a carveout that specifies supported model variants and pinned versions. DocuSign link should include the exact credit formula.

Next steps: Diego — please confirm you will communicate these conditions to Pylon and request an SOW signature via DocuSign. Create INFRA ticket (INFRA-1123) to track runbook implementation and SRE on-call assignment.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1123
- DocuSign template: https://app.docusign.com/documents/ABC123-pylon

Subject: Re: Uptime & latency commitments for enterprise plan - Pylon

Hi Aisha — thank you for your patience and for sharing Pylon's proposed SLA. We reviewed this internally and can agree to a customer-specific commitment with the following agreed terms: 

Summary of agreed commitment:
- Deployment: Dedicated reserved capacity (per-customer GPU pool) with cross-AZ redundancy.
- Uptime: Commitment of 99.995% (annual) for the dedicated pool subject to the scheduled maintenance windows below.
- Latency: Target p95 token-generation latency < 150ms for the workload profile you provided (avg ~512 tokens) when using the agreed model variant and pinned model versions.
- Maintenance windows: Two scheduled windows per quarter, max 2 hours each. Unexpected maintenance will be measured against the SLO and handled per runbook.
- Financial exposure: Service credit cap set to 3 months of recurring fees. Any customer request above this cap will require VP approval.

Next steps:
1) We will send an updated SOW and DocuSign package this afternoon (DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/documents/ABC123-pylon).
2) Please confirm the billing contact and an initial kickoff date.
3) Once SOW is signed, INFRA-1123 will track runbook implementation and SRE onboarding.

Attachments included: pylon-sow-template.docx, availability-runbook-draft.md

If this matches Pylon's expectations, please sign the DocuSign package and we'll schedule a technical kickoff with SRE and your engineering lead (Michael Yuan).

Best,
